BiblicalUsage: Agathopoiia is well-doing — the life of doing good, named as a single thing — and it appears once, in Peter's word to suffering believers: 'let them that suffer according to the will of God commit the keeping of their souls to him in well doing, as unto a faithful Creator.' The word gathers a whole life of good deeds into one act of trust: keep doing good, and leave your soul with the God who made it.
TheologicalSignificance: Its meaning is narrow and practical, and any larger lesson comes from the story or command it appears in, not from the word itself; in this case, the verse is 1 Peter 4:19.
